scenes.conflict: Jamie wants to prove they can solve it alone, while Marty doubts notes from someone who has never competed at his level; ARCADE-X's repeating prompts tempt them to play.
scenes.goal: Work out whether ARCADE-X's strange prompts can explain the new street changes.
scenes.outcome: Marty agrees to demonstrate the rhythm, and Jamie withholds the notebook's uncertain entries, setting up a risky test instead of a careful comparison.
scenes.summary: At Starway Arcade, Jamie shows Marty the blank ARCADE-X cabinet and admits the score prompts seemed to behave like instructions. Jamie keeps their detailed notebook hidden, while Marty recognizes a familiar competitive rhythm in the remaining prompts.
scenes.title: A Scoreboard with No Cabinet

scenes.conflict: Disconnecting now would stabilize the network but erase the live route needed to locate the source.
scenes.goal: Find a measurable path through the anomalous calls before the exchange cutoff.
scenes.outcome: Ruth delays the cutoff long enough to investigate, but sets a firm deadline for a useful trace.
scenes.summary: At the switching exchange, Ruth compares the anomalous call records with paper route maps and finds the live route is still traceable. She receives pressure to disconnect it before the shifting calls spread further.
scenes.title: The One-Day Cutoff

scenes.conflict: Marty's pride pushes him to repeat the sequence, and ARCADE-X's prompts exploit that competitive instinct.
scenes.goal: Capture a repeatable pattern that links the cabinet's prompts to the city's changes.
scenes.outcome: The play produces a new burst of score tones and a route disturbance, proving the pattern matters while making another demonstration too dangerous.
scenes.summary: Marty demonstrates the score rhythm at the arcade, hoping his old timing still holds. Jamie records the tones, but the repeated play coincides with a fresh street-routing anomaly.
scenes.title: One More Demonstration

scenes.conflict: Each fresh score pattern shifts the calls, while the cutoff order leaves little time to compare readings.
scenes.goal: Use the surge to narrow the live signal to a traceable branch.
scenes.outcome: Ruth identifies the underpass pay phone as the clearest next trace point and keeps the route connected for one attempt.
scenes.summary: Ruth's test set registers a measurable surge as calls reroute through the exchange. She marks the changing branch on her paper map and realizes that the route is moving too quickly for routine procedure alone.
scenes.title: Warm Relays

scenes.conflict: Club members want a final high-score attempt, and Jamie's guarded notebook leaves contradictions unresolved.
scenes.goal: Compare the club's observations with Jamie's score records without starting another session.
scenes.outcome: Arla cancels the run and gives Jamie her complete chart; Jamie admits which notebook entries are guesses, allowing the group to plan a cautious trace.
scenes.summary: At the arcade, Arla brings the Last Life Club's handwritten observations to Jamie and Marty. She initially wants one more group run, but their notes connect repeated play sessions with the street changes.
scenes.title: The Club's Route Chart

scenes.conflict: Jamie has acted on an unverified entry, and ARCADE-X's repeated tones threaten to draw Marty into another play pattern.
scenes.goal: Use the pay phone and score records to identify which route carries ARCADE-X's signal.
scenes.outcome: The loop exposes Jamie's mistake; Jamie shares the full notebook, Marty refuses to repeat the challenge, and Ruth records a surge that points toward the relay roof.
scenes.summary: At the underpass pay phone, Ruth tests the live line while Jamie compares the charts and Marty watches the changing lane squares. Jamie's private route guess sends them back toward the entrance in a short loop.
scenes.title: The Checkerboard Trap

scenes.conflict: The signal is intermittent, and another repeated pattern could strengthen the maze before Ruth finishes tracing it.
scenes.goal: Correlate the roof's signal reading with the underpass surge and locate the route's endpoint.
scenes.outcome: The readings show the live route returns toward Starway Arcade's service connection; the trio can make one final trace before Ruth must disconnect it.
scenes.summary: At Channel Nine Roof, Ruth compares the signal burst with the relay test monitor. Jamie and Marty match its timing to the club's chart without playing the sequence, while Ruth annotates the route on her map.
scenes.title: Digits in the Snow

acts.title: Routes That Refuse to Stay Put

scenes.conflict: ARCADE-X needs a human-entered pattern to shape its signal, Marty is tempted to answer the challenge, and Ruth must decide whether to keep the route live.
scenes.goal: Capture the final surge's route information without giving ARCADE-X another full play sequence.
scenes.outcome: Marty refuses the challenge; Jamie and Ruth use the existing tones and test readings to mark the return route, but Ruth warns that the connection can remain live only briefly.
scenes.summary: The trio returns to the underpass to confirm the route. ARCADE-X sends its strongest score prompt through the pay phone, and its tones target Marty's competitive pride as Ruth's test set registers a fresh surge.
scenes.title: ARCADE-X's Challenge

scenes.conflict: ARCADE-X repeats its lure as the signal surges; Ruth's cutoff deadline is near, and an unverified disconnection could leave the route active elsewhere.
scenes.goal: Verify that the cabinet's service connection is the source before disconnecting the route.
scenes.outcome: Ruth confirms the service port is the source. Jamie shares the final sequence instead of claiming certainty alone, and Ruth disconnects the cabinet from the live phone route.
scenes.summary: Back at Starway Arcade, the team follows Ruth's marked route to ARCADE-X's wired service connection. Jamie matches the prompt to the shared chart, Marty identifies the timing variation that would otherwise invite another repetition, and Ruth confirms the live line with her test set.
scenes.title: The Service Port

scenes.conflict: The trio must distinguish a genuine stop from a temporary lull before declaring the route safe.
scenes.goal: Confirm that disconnecting the service port has stopped ARCADE-X's changes from traveling through the network.
scenes.outcome: Ruth verifies the line is quiet and keeps the paper map as a record; the city is no longer receiving new score patterns.
scenes.summary: At the switching exchange, Ruth checks the route after the disconnection. The score-like surges have stopped, and the mapped calls no longer shift between branches.
scenes.title: A Quiet Exchange

scenes.conflict: The club still wants a triumphant final run, while Jamie and Marty know repeated play helped feed the signal.
scenes.goal: Preserve what the group learned and keep the club from restarting the high-score ritual.
scenes.outcome: Arla leads the club in recording observations rather than playing; Jamie shares credit for the chart, and Marty accepts a role as coach instead of champion.
scenes.summary: Back at Starway Arcade, Arla organizes the club's notes with Jamie's notebook. Marty helps the players observe the quiet cabinet without turning the crisis into another contest.
scenes.title: A Better Kind of Score

logline: With Bellwether Telephone ready to cut the unstable route, mallrat hacker Jamie, former arcade champion Marty, and lineman Ruth must decode ARCADE-X's final human-entered score pattern and locate its source before the city's streets become a permanent 8-bit maze.
theme: A shared effort matters more than a solitary high score.
title: High Score Apocalypse
